subject: general
question: Two resistors, A (20 Ω) and B (40 Ω), are connected in parallel. The combination is connected to a 6 V battery. The currents in A and B are respectively ________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.3 A and 0.15 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In a **parallel circuit**, the voltage across each branch is the same; hence **VA=VB=6 V**.
 
• By **Ohm’s law** (*I = V/R*): IA = 6/20 = **0.30 A**, IB = 6/40 = **0.15 A** → matches option 3.
 
• Currents in parallel branches are **inversely proportional to resistances**; here IA/IB = RB/RA = 40/20 = 2, consistent with 0.30 A vs 0.15 A.
 
• Check: **Rₑq = (R₁R₂)/(R₁+R₂) = 13.33 Ω**, so total current = 6/13.33 ≈ 0.45 A = 0.30 + 0.15 A.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm’s law forms**: V = IR, I = V/R, R = V/I—fundamental for branch-current calculations. 
 
• In parallel, the **total current equals the sum** of branch currents (Kirchhoff’s Current Law).
 
• **Equivalent resistance in parallel** is always less than the smallest branch; for two resistors use *product-over-sum*.
 
• **Power in a resistor**: P = VI = I²R = V²/R; at 6 V, PA=1.8 W and PB=0.9 W, so the lower resistance dissipates more power.
